* The history and present state of electricity: with original experiments by Joseph Priestley
Call Number: QC516.P95 1769
Publication Date: 1769
Joseph Priestley (1733-1804) was a chemist, theologian and philosopher and will be known by most as the discoverer of oxygen, but he is also considered the first true historian of the science of electricity. His book, The History and Present State of Electricity, first published in 1767, was encouraged by his friend Benjamin Franklin. It brought together historic and contemporary knowledge of electricity, including electrical machines. The figures shown here are of hand cranked electrical wheels by a Dr. Watson and a Mr. Wilson, and Priestly remarks of figure 2:
“One of the most complete machines, and one that had the greatest power of any that I have seen, except my own, is of this construction.”
Priestley also added his own discoveries, such as the conductive properties of charcoal. The account of Franklins famous key experiment within The History and Present State of Electricity is described thoroughly and is generally considered the authoritative record.
